case_studies.abstract: Recent position papers argue that the classical aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty framework is insufficient for interactive large language model (LLM) agents and call for underspecification-aware, decomposed, and communicable uncertainty representations that can unlock new agent capabilities such as proactive clarification seeking and shared mental-model building. case_studies.title: AgentFinVQA: A Deployable Multi-Agent Pipeline for Auditable Financial Chart QA
case_studies.abstract: Financial chart question answering in regulated settings demands more than accuracy: practitioners must know which answers to trust before acting on them, and many institutions cannot send client data to external model providers. Yet existing chart-QA agents are accuracy-focused and opaque, and most assume proprietary API access; to our knowledge, none combines auditability with on-premise deployability without significant accuracy compromise. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of trustworthy financial chart question answering in regulated settings by building AgentFinVQA, a deployable multi-agent pipeline. AgentFinVQA allows for auditable and on-premise deployment without significant accuracy compromise. The result is a more reliable and transparent financial chart QA system.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage financial data infrastructure, here is what to do: check if your organisation uses external model providers for financial chart QA, consider deploying AgentFinVQA for on-premise and auditable solutions, review your current QA pipeline for potential integration with AgentFinVQA.

case_studies.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents are increasingly being used to automate multi-step engineering work flows by interacting with software tools, interpreting intermediate results, and autonomously planning subsequent actions. Power system dynamic studies represent a particularly promising yet largely unexplored application domain for these agents. Unlike static computational tasks, dynamic studies often require more time on model parameter calibration, engineering judgment, and decision making under constrained action spaces. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of automating complex engineering workflows in power system dynamic studies by introducing a benchmark for agentic AI. The result is a potentially more efficient way to automate multi-step engineering tasks.

case_studies.title: Multi-View Decompilation for LLM-Based Malware Classification
case_studies.abstract: Malware analysts often inspect compiled binaries through decompiled pseudo-C, when source code is unavailable. Recent work suggests that large language models (LLMs) can assist this process by classifying decompiled code as benign or malicious, but existing pipelines typically rely on a single decompiler view. case_studies.title: Formal Verification of Learned Multi-Agent Communication Policies via Decision Tree Distillation
case_studies.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables agents to develop coordination strategies through emergent communication, but neural policies lack the formal safety guarantees required for safety-critical robotic deployment in drone swarms and autonomous vehicle fleets. We present the first end-to-end framework for safety verification of learned multi-agent communication policies through policy abstraction: neural policies are distilled into interpretable decision trees, then formally verified, with empirical validation confirming that verified safety properties transfer to original networks
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of ensuring safety guarantees in multi-agent reinforcement learning, building a framework to verify learned communication policies through decision tree distillation, and resulting in verified safety properties that transfer to original networks. The researchers built an end-to-end framework for safety verification of learned policies. This is not directly applicable to cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.abstract: This paper develops a general framework for analyzing multi-agent systems with feedback loops between agents actions and collective observations. The framework is built on two fundamental agent-level variables: power, which measures agent influence on collective outcomes, and response functions, which determine how agents react to observations. We derive how macroscopic properties, including total power, useful power, entropy, order, fragility, and mobility, emerge from these two variables of heterogeneous agents. case_studies.title: UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents
case_studies.abstract: Context-heavy agents place unusual pressure on the key-value (KV) cache: long prefixes are reused across many short turns, while concurrency determines whether the serving system can keep GPUs utilized. We study 4-bit KV-cache compression for this setting, using TurboQuant-style rotation and codebook quantization as a quality anchor and vLLM FP8 KV caching as the deployment anchor. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of optimizing key-value cache performance for context-heavy agents, building a 4-bit KV caching system called UltraQuant, which resulted in improved cache compression and serving throughput. UltraQuant uses TurboQuant-style rotation and codebook quantization to achieve high-quality caching. This research is relevant to IT engineers managing cloud infrastructure that supports AI workloads.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for AI workloads, here is what to do: check your key-value cache configuration, consider implementing 4-bit KV caching like UltraQuant, and evaluate the impact on your serving throughput and task quality. This may require adjustments to your GPU utilization and concurrency settings. If your organization uses context-heavy agents, review your cache compression strategy to optimize performance.
